title: Contrastive training, in one matrix
sub: A toy CLIP: similarity between 6 held-out images (rows) and their captions (columns).

frames.caption: Six held-out image-caption pairs that training never sees. Each cell is the cosine similarity between image i's embedding and caption j's. Before training the two encoders are random, so the matrix is noise; the best-matching caption in each row (green if right, red if wrong) is right only by luck.

CLIP-style training: for each batch of matched pairs, push every image towards its own caption and away from the other captions in the batch (and the same for captions), using a softmax over each row and column with a temperature τ = 0.1.
The diagonal lights up: five of the six images now score their own caption highest, even though these pairs were never trained on. The encoders have learned a shared space.
Every image's best match is its own caption. Zero-shot classification works the same way: embed the image, embed captions like "a photo of a dog" for each class, and pick the most similar.
